newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH INDUSTRY UNION WANTS LOW INFLATION PAY DEAL.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH INDUSTRY UNION WANTS LOW INFLATION PAY DEAL.

text.p: Finland should try to maintain steady growth and low inflation since stability at home will be crucial when Finland steps into an EMU-era full of unknowns, the leader of a big Finnish industrial trade union said on Friday.

"Finland's transfer into the EMU-era will entail many unknown and unpredictable matters," Helena Rissanen, chairman of the Union of Salaried Employees in Industry (STL), said in the summary of a prepared speech at the union's 80-year anniversary.
"Because of this, we must ensure domestic political stability. We must ensure economic growth by simultaneously keeping inflation in check and interest rates low," she said.
Growth and low inflation and interest rates were important for employment, Rissanen said.
In the coming autumn's incomes settlement talks ahead of the expiry at end-January 1998 of current agreements, Rissanen said everyone should look beyond branch or political interests.
No branch-specific problems were so big that they could not be solved, if employers, showed willingness, she said.
"The government must participate in building a comprehensive incomes settlement," Rissanen said, adding a broad pay deal would require an index clause.
The government should also put together a concrete stimulation package to boost employment, she said, but gave no details.

Also speaking at the STL anniversary, director Seppo Riski at the Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT) said labour market policy should focus on keeping costs under control and on the creation of flexible operations.
"This affects companies' competitiveness and ... whether investments in production will be made in Finland or outside Finland," Riski said.
